doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Growing caseload and hiring Lauren Roberts
summary: The Foundation grows from 35 to 150 musicians as she makes calls; she recruits Vassar graduate Lauren Roberts via harmonica teacher Adam Gussow.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: We didn’t know what we were doing. I want to say at this point, and introduce the next great person who came into our midst. Not just Jarrett Lilien, who ended up saving the day and then becoming our president, who has been my partner in this for years. But Lauren Roberts, who... When they handed me the keys to this place with the $7,000 in the bank, I was the only employee—that was going to be that. I needed someone. I couldn’t do this alone. We were getting to the point where we were starting to see now, from 35 musicians a year, 50 musicians, then it went to 150...
Is that because people were finding out about the service, or because of demographics, the aging population...
They never had someone really making the calls and doing the work.
So you started very proactively making phone calls and...

Well, you’d hear about... Sure. Someone would tell me someone is having a hard time, and then that person would generally know someone, and then they would know someone. We got to all be so close, and it was such a feeling of family and of trust. It was a beautiful thing. I want to introduce Lauren Roberts to this. She was a 22-year-old Vassar student, who was just graduating. The one man who gave me a harmonica lesson, this great guy, Adam Gussow, was teaching there, and he was now moving to Mississippi, and he said, “I have a student who I think would be great to help you.” I met her, fell in love immediately, and the two of us were like 12 hours a day... We would get locked in the building at the union. There were moments where we would get locked in; they’d forget we were in the office—at night. Those were crazy days, but we got a lot done. And she helped me put on the Great Night in Harlem.
